hub_identity.reservation_rule: Create the ticket under registry lock before writing runners, artifacts, data, or logs. Existing IDs are rejected across registry, JSONL, tickets, logs, artifacts, data, and runners.

hypothesis: Envelope v2 for the accepted source-priority allocator changes exactly one specification versus the rejected v1: the kill switch measures realized drawdown against the realized-equity peak (bucket plus cumulative realized PnL) with a 15pct threshold sized about 1.5x the worst healthy-window giveback, instead of 8pct of the fixed bucket which false-triggered on profit giveback; all other envelope terms (8 concurrent, 4k USD notional, 32k USD bucket, ADV floor, next-open no-chase, zero displacement) are unchanged, and the gate passes only if every canonical window keeps positive EV delta, EV retention stays >=80pct, and the kill switch never triggers.

prediction.confidence_reason: v1 false-triggered on profit giveback because 8pct of fixed bucket sits inside normal realized variation (healthy windows hit 6.6-10.9pct); the equity-peak basis at 15pct sits outside every observed healthy giveback. Caveat: threshold calibrated on the same frozen windows, so the in-sample no-false-trigger check is partially circular; binding validation is OOS plus forward rows. steady-state concurrency is about 9; production daily already caps open positions at 8 while accepted replay never enforced the cap. The allocator ranks by ex-ante priority, so skipped marginal trades should be lower value, but if the skipped tail carries the PnL or mid_weak drawdown crosses 8pct of the bucket the declared envelope fails.

production_impact.shared_policy_note: EXECUTION_ENVELOPE, evaluate_kill_switch_state, and apply_execution_envelope_to_trades added to the shared allocator helper; daily snapshot now exposes execution_envelope and kill_switch_state. Selection, ranking, sizing, exits, and order behavior unchanged; sleeve remains default-off paper.
remaining_live_blockers: genuine forward closed rows under the unified universe

post_run_reflection.why_result_happened: The allocator selects at most one ex-ante ranked row per day, so the concurrency cap mostly trims overlapping tail entries; retention and kill-switch outcomes quantify exactly what production can execute.
post_run_reflection.forbidden_near_neighbor_retry: Do not sweep bucket size, concurrency cap, kill-switch threshold, or ADV floor on the frozen windows to manufacture a pass.
post_run_reflection.new_evidence_required: Genuine forward closed rows under the unified universe plus replay-vs-forward parity; then live pilot sizing is an operator config decision behind the kill switch.

summary: Production daily caps open positions at max_active_positions=8 while the accepted replay never enforced concurrency; this gate measures the constrained replay so accepted metrics and production behavior match.
